findings.statement: The checker contradicted the author. On the first executed run, the declared key-index mutation SURVIVED the original MaskRoundTrip invariant with exit 0 over the identical 3,618-state space: XOR with any fixed index function is an involution, so a round-trip-only check is blind to key ALIGNMENT. The invariant was partially vacuous and its declared falsification note was wrong. Fixed in the MODEL by restating the mask equation independently (MaskEquationReference) and checking the transform against it; the same mutation now dies with exit 12. The port's mask function was never implicated.

The port checks the 125-octet control-payload limit twice; the second comparison (decoded length vs 125 at the length site) is UNREACHABLE, because a control frame surviving the extended-marker gate has an inline marker and therefore a length of at most 125. ControlOverLimitRejectedAtBaseHeader holds, confirming every over-limit control frame is rejected at consumed offset 2. Shipped Java's gate has the same shape (drafts/Draft_6455.java:617-620), so the port's second comparison is defensive depth that matches the fidelity authority.

The port's normalize_send_close_code rewrites 1015 to 1005 but omits Java's accompanying reason-clearing side effect (framing/CloseFrame.java:184). TLC shows the omission is observationally inert: TlsErrorSendAlwaysRejectedAs1002 holds over both reason kinds because every route (1005 with a reason, 1005 without, un-normalized 1015) reports 1002 and emits no frame.

Shipped Java's close() catches the InvalidDataException from the close frame's isValid, calls flushAndClose, and sets readyState = CLOSING (WebSocketImpl.java:488-503), so a Java endpoint ENTERS CLOSING on an illegal local close code. The port returns the typed failure, emits no frame, and does not transition -- matching internal/corpora/derive.go sendClose, which the US-016 owner amendment names as binding. The divergence from raw Java has NO behavior-delta-ledger record. Whether one is owed is an owner call, not this worker's; recorded rather than invented or ignored.

Strengthening it to assert acceptance immediately surfaced two genuine breakages in this same round that the weak form would have waved through, so the finding paid for itself before I finished acting on it.

blocking_1_resolution_detail.name_vocabulary_closed: mrDriverDigestNames enumerates the permitted names per kind: tool -> tla2tools.jar; manifest -> the canonical manifest basename; staged/pristine -> <Module>.tla and <Module>.cfg for every module ModelResultsBindings declares. Any other name is rejected, so a substituted or extra artifact cannot ride along under a legitimate kind.
blocking_1_resolution_detail.grammar_closed: The scan is line-oriented: every line beginning with DIGEST must match the strict pattern. A malformed line is rejected rather than silently skipped, which a whole-text FindAllStringSubmatch sweep did. A line the parser cannot read is a line nothing checks.
blocking_1_resolution_detail.manifest_path_bound: New constant ModelMutationsPath pins the canonical driver input (assurance/formal/model-mutations.json, the exact path cmd/tlcdriver reads). The recorded path must equal it, so a byte-identical decoy at another path is refused -- previously any path whose bytes hashed correctly was accepted.

honesty_notes_round_6: BLOCKING 2 is the worst thing I have done in this lane. Every other finding was a check that was too weak; this was a STATEMENT that was untrue. I asserted a completeness property over a set of tests without counting them, in a receipt whose entire purpose is to be trusted about exactly that kind of claim. The six cases even had the detail field sitting unused, so the evidence that the conversion was incomplete was in the diff I wrote.
The rule I should have followed is the one this lane already enforces on the models: do not assert a property you have not executed. I applied it to invariants and not to my own prose.

BLOCKING 1 is the third round in a row where a vocabulary I had just closed turned out to be closed at only one level. Kind, then name, then grammar. Each time I fixed the level I was shown and did not ask what the next level down was.

Known open items are listed with locations and exploitability rather than as a vague caveat, because a reader inheriting this needs the boundary, not reassurance. Four of the six were verified against the validator source in this session; two are structural observations.

Final honest summary of six rounds: the evidence artifacts (two models, 25/25 executed kills, the qualification stance) have been stable and unchallenged since round 2. Everything since has been hardening the machinery that guards them, and every round found more. The artifacts are sound; the validator is better than it was and is not finished, and the list above says where it stops.
